headline: The catalog's size floor is a fixed pixel count, not a physical size; the observed size distribution is nearly universal in D/pixel across all resolutions, so hollow SIZES in this catalog are set by imaging resolution, not by hollow physics, over 0.1-10 km.

evidence.upper_rolloff: tail slope in pixel units steepens 3.2 -> 3.9 -> 4.6 for xmin 40/60/80 px, i.e. the detector also has an upper size limit near 100-200 px

non_identifiability: A scale-free intrinsic law times a completeness window in D/px predicts exactly the observed universality, so the intrinsic slope and the completeness curve cannot be separated from single-coverage data. A joint fit converged (alpha 4.0, D50 53 px) but FAILED validation against per-bin quantiles; it is not used.
how_the_degeneracy_was_broken: Repeat coverage. Every searched NAC frame covering a hollow is a detection trial; 147,704 hollow-frame pairs over 9,803 hollows. Fitted with a binomial likelihood conditional on >=1 detection per hollow (the naive fit is biased by that selection, which made the apparent per-frame rate fall from 0.43 to 0.06 with the number of covering frames).
per_frame_form: p(x,inc)=p_max*Phi((ln x-ln x50)/sigma_lo)*(1-Phi((ln x-ln x_hi)/sigma_hi))*exp(b_inc*(inc-60)/25); x=D_eq/px

implied_catalog_completeness.reading: even a well-resolved hollow is in the catalog with probability of order 0.2-0.3 at typical northern coverage; the catalog samples the tip of a much larger population, and north-south completeness ratios exceed 10x below 1 km

what_downstream_tracks_must_do: size fits: weight each hollow by 1/C(D, site) (Vmax analog) or fit with the per-site completeness as the censoring model; never fit raw sizes
spatial statistics: the null intensity is coverage x completeness, from completeness_10ppd.npz
prediction: 'large' for the south is the size at which southern C(D) becomes non-negligible; degrade the north to the southern frame distribution before training
